traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960), as Senecio jacobaea: stems 20 cm to 1 m tall. The typical value is the one the plant was drawn at before, inside the source's range.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960), as Senecio jacobaea: leaves 4 cm to 20 cm long.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: an invasive, poisonous herb with ragged, deeply cut leaves and flat-topped clusters of yellow daisy heads. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 0.9 m tall at 4 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: dark green leaves; yellow heads.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.life_span.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Senecio jacobaea (p. 450): biennial or rather short-lived perennial.

traits.woodiness.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, S. jacobaea (p. 450): a biennial or short-lived perennial herb with a taproot.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, S. jacobaea (p. 450): leaves about 4-20 cm long and 2-6 cm wide.

traits.leaf_division.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, S. jacobaea (p. 450): one blade, 2-3 times pinnatifid.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, S. jacobaea (p. 450): leaves mostly 2-3 times pinnatifid.

traits.division_pattern.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, S. jacobaea (p. 450): pinnatifid.

traits.division_order.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, S. jacobaea (p. 450): mostly 2-3 times pinnatifid.

traits.inflorescence.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, S. jacobaea (p. 450): several to rather many heads in a short broad (flat-topped) array.

traits.capitulum_kind.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, S. jacobaea (p. 450): rays commonly about 13.

traits.involucre_height_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, S. jacobaea (p. 450): involucre about 4 mm high.

traits.involucre_diameter_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, S. jacobaea (p. 450): the disc about 7-10 mm wide (the disc's width, used for the involucre's).

traits.phyllaries.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, S. jacobaea (p. 450): involucral bracts about 13, over 1 mm wide, generally dark-tipped.

traits.ray_florets.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, S. jacobaea (p. 450): rays commonly about 13.

traits.ray_length_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, S. jacobaea (p. 450): rays mostly 4-10 mm long.

traits.flowering_months.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, S. jacobaea (p. 450): July to September.

appearance.organs.leaf.shape.note: The blade drawn as a twice-divided leaf (spec rework E1), Abrams and Ferris's bipinnatifid blade of toothed, cut segments: about 5 pairs of primary segments, each cut into about 5 lobes, the end segment largest, by eye from photographs; its pattern from its characters by the rules at the flowering plants. Its segments run together along a winged rachis (confluent 0.6, by eye): the flora's blade is cut, not divided into leaflets, and the rule at the flowering plants that runs them together reads only a dissected one. Before, a five-lobed blade.

appearance.organs.basal.shape.note: The basal blade drawn as the stem's (spec rework E1), on a longer stalk, by eye from photographs.
